blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic working capital optimisation is not the same thing as cost cutting. It is the patient search for cash that is already earned but not yet available — trapped in inventory that moves slowly, in receivables that are agreed but unpaid, in supplier terms shorter than they could reasonably be.

A senior treasurer approaches this as a portfolio exercise. Inventory is reviewed not by line but by velocity: which SKUs are cash sinks, which are cash engines, and what would happen if the slowest twenty per cent were managed differently? Receivables are reviewed not by customer but by aging cohort: which cohorts are drifting, and why? Payables are reviewed not as a moral question but as a policy one: what terms do market peers actually take, and are we leaving capacity on the table?

Only after all three levers have been assessed does external financing come into the conversation. Rarely is the answer only one of the three. More often, it is a deliberate, coordinated pull on all of them — a quiet release of cash that did not need to be borrowed because it had been there all along.

items.q: According to the text, how does working capital optimisation differ from cost cutting?
options: It searches for cash that is already earned but not yet available
It reduces headcount rather than spending
items.why: "It is the patient search for cash that is already earned but not yet available" — não é corte, é liberação do que já existe.

items.q: How is inventory reviewed by a senior treasurer?
items.why: "Inventory is reviewed not by line but by velocity" — separa cash sinks de cash engines.

items.q: When does external financing enter the conversation?
options: Before any internal lever is assessed
As the first and preferred option
Only after all three levers have been assessed
Instead of touching receivables or payables
items.why: "Only after all three levers have been assessed does external financing come into the conversation."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The three levers should be pulled together, not one at a time
Borrowing should be the first move to free up cash
Payables terms should be benchmarked against peers
Slow-moving inventory ties up recoverable cash
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata o financiamento externo como último recurso — o dinheiro já estava dentro de casa.

items.q: The phrase "cash that did not need to be borrowed because it had been there all along" suggests that…
options: companies routinely overlook cash trapped inside their own operations
external debt is always cheaper than internal cash
coordinated action is impossible in practice
items.why: Inferência: o caixa 'preso' em estoque, recebíveis e prazos é subestimado — está lá, à espera de ser liberado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando o programa de liberação de caixa ao CFO. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you for the time. Before we talk about any new facility from the banks, I want to walk you through what we already own but cannot yet spend.

We ran the inventory not line by line, but by velocity. The slowest fifth of our SKUs is sitting on roughly forty days of cash — those are the sinks. A handful of fast movers, by contrast, are pure engines. If we manage that bottom cohort differently, we free a meaningful sum without touching a single supplier.

On receivables, I stopped looking at customer names and started looking at aging cohorts. Two cohorts have quietly drifted out past their terms, and no one flagged it because each account, on its own, looked fine. On payables, we are simply more generous than the market. Our peers take longer terms than we do, so we are leaving real capacity on the table.

Here is my recommendation. We pull all three levers in parallel, not one after another. Rarely is the answer just one of them. Do that, and the cash release covers the shortfall — with nothing borrowed, because it was ours all along.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Harry want to cover BEFORE discussing a new bank facility?
options: The cost of the last audit
Cash the company already owns but cannot yet spend
A new hiring plan for the treasury team
The exchange-rate forecast for the quarter
items.why: "I want to walk you through what we already own but cannot yet spend."

items.q: How much cash is the slowest fifth of SKUs tying up?
options: About twenty per cent of revenue
items.why: "The slowest fifth of our SKUs is sitting on roughly forty days of cash."

items.q: Why did no one flag the drifting receivables cohorts?
options: The customers had strong credit ratings
Each account, on its own, looked fine
The terms had recently been renegotiated
items.why: "no one flagged it because each account, on its own, looked fine" — só o padrão por coorte revela o problema.

items.q: What does Harry imply about the company's payables terms?
options: They are aggressive and risk damaging supplier relations
They are more generous than the market, leaving capacity unused
They are already the tightest in the sector
They cannot be changed without board approval
items.why: Inferência: "we are simply more generous than the market… leaving real capacity on the table" — dá para alongar prazos como os pares.

items.q: What is the core of Harry's recommendation?
options: Fix receivables only, since it is the fastest lever
Pull all three levers in parallel, rarely just one
Delay any action until the next quarter
items.why: "We pull all three levers in parallel, not one after another. Rarely is the answer just one of them."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Those slow-moving lines are pure cash sinks." A cash sink is…
options: a product or asset that ties up cash without releasing it
a bank account earning high interest
a supplier offering long payment terms
a customer who always pays early
items.why: Cash sink = sugador de caixa: prende dinheiro sem devolver.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We review inventory by ___, so we can tell the fast sellers from the ones gathering dust."
items.why: Velocity = velocidade de giro do estoque — o critério da lição.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Two ___ have drifted past their terms, even though every single account looked healthy."
items.why: Aging cohort = coorte de vencimento; o problema só aparece agrupando os recebíveis por idade.

items.q: "By paying suppliers faster than everyone else, we are leaving capacity on the table." This means we are…
options: failing to use room we could safely exploit
breaching a covenant with the bank
items.why: Leaving capacity on the table = deixar capacidade sem uso — dá para alongar prazos sem risco.

items.q: "A handful of fast movers are pure cash engines." A cash engine is…
options: an item that generates and turns cash quickly
items.why: Cash engine = motor de caixa: gira rápido e gera dinheiro, o oposto do cash sink.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de tesouraria e gestão de caixa. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the cash release programme." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new payables policy across all business units." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Procurement pushed back on extending supplier terms." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed the collections plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Squeezing one small supplier will not move the needle on the cash gap." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
